reason: Both share the same broken structure. The four steps are scattered down the strip out of order (3, 2, 4, 1), split apart by the jar and the CTA, and their step text is tiny and hard to read at this size. The pink circle is cropped awkwardly at the bottom-right, and the bottom 20% is left almost empty while the headline fills the top. A edges ahead only because its logo is larger and more legible; B's logo is very small, though its jar fills the width a little better.

Both use the same broken layout: the 'Read 2,400 Reviews' CTA sits at the top above the quote, which reverses the reading order. The pink circle that framed the bottle is detached and clipped in the bottom-right corner, the quote mark floats with a large gap above the headline, and the testimonial is set too small to be the focal point while the bottle dominates. The only difference is that B sits about 23px higher, which leaves slightly more dead space at the bottom. That is not a meaningful difference.

Both share the same broken structure: the legal block sits at the very top above the headline, so the reading order is wrong; the small 'CLINICALLY TESTED' eyebrow has become a huge letterspaced line under the subhead that competes with the headline; the logo is pushed to the bottom corner; and the jar is cut off from the leaf image. A's legal text is unreadably tiny, but its subhead lines up with the headline's left edge. B's legal text is slightly larger but runs almost to the canvas edges, and its subhead is indented about 15px off the headline's edge, which is a visible misalignment, so A is marginally better.

A: the Pre-order CTA sits top-left beside the headphones as if it were a tag, so the reading order starts with the action. The teal disc has come loose from the headphones and dropped to the bottom-left, where it covers the tiny, unreadable OBSIDIAN logo. The centred price also clashes with the left-aligned headline. B: it has the same problems: the CTA is on top, the disc is stranded, and the logo is small and sits on the disc. The left-aligned headline and body copy also break its centred axis, and the body line is jammed under the headline. Still, B's CTA, headphones and price share one centred column, so it reads as slightly more deliberate than A's arbitrary side-by-side top row.

A: the spec stats, subtitle and legal line are scattered down the left in a jumbled order at microscopic, unreadable sizes. The Pre-order CTA is a tiny pill, '-38 dB' floats alone under the headline, and the headphones are clipped at the right edge with the teal circle knocked off-centre. B has the same broken scatter (legal text mixed in with the stats, a buried CTA, clipped headphones), and its stat sizes vary at random ('6 mics', '10 min' and '-38 dB' are large while '40 h' and 'BT 5.4' are tiny), with '250 g' jammed under 'charge for 5 hours'. Still, B is slightly more legible.

A's left edges don't line up: the quote mark (~x80), headline and logo (~x57) and the review credit and rating (~x43) sit on three different edges. A's stack also floats high and leaves about 130px of dead space at the bottom. B puts the quote mark, headline, credit and rating on one left edge and spreads the content better down the tall canvas, though the logo is still indented. In both, the credit, rating and logo shrank to tiny, weak text, and the gaps between blocks are loose and uneven.

The two layouts are nearly identical and share the same flaws. The headline sits right against the left edge (about 6px in) while the CTA is inset about 16px, so they don't line up. The OBSIDIAN logo sits under the headline instead of leading as it did in the original. The three elements float with no grid, and about 110px at the top is empty. A also leaves about 110px empty below the CTA. B places the CTA lower, which fills the height a little better, but it widens the gap between headline and logo to about 190px, so the elements still look scattered rather than grouped.

Both have the same main faults: '$3' now sits above '2 FOR', so the offer reads backwards. The FIZZBANG! logo is shrunk into a stray pill at the bottom that lines up with nothing. The Find a Store CTA floats alone in the top-right corner, away from its copy. A also leaves a ~160px dead gap between the can (pushed far left) and the text column, while B pulls the can closer for a slightly more cohesive group, though it has a wide empty left margin and a loose gap under '2 FOR'.

A: the headline and subcopy share a left edge, but the CTA is centred on a different axis. The FIZZBANG logo and the can have shrunk to tiny illegible specks at the bottom, which kills the brand, and there's a big dead area above the controller. B has the same tiny unreadable logo and can, and it adds a clear alignment error: the subcopy is indented about 50px from the headline and runs almost to the right edge. Its oversized controller and empty bottom third make it the less balanced of the two.

Neither candidate is ready to ship; A is the less bad of two. A: the yellow circle has come off the can and sits alone in the top-right corner, with the Try It button half covering it and almost touching the right edge. The tagline is pushed down against the bottom edge, well away from the headline. The headline floats in empty space in the middle, and the can is pressed to the top and bottom edges. B: it repeats the same broken composition, with the circle split off and cropped at the right edge and the CTA overlapping it. On top of that, its 'Zero sugar, all bang.' tagline has shrunk to unreadable micro-text in the bottom-left corner, so it fails on readability as well.

A: the big opening quote mark is now a tiny glyph floating above the text, the attribution is spaced out and nearly as heavy as the quote (hierarchy inverted), the one-line quote is small and the 'GALLERY' tag looks garbled; the left margin and logo spacing still work, though. B has the same tiny quote mark and oversized attribution, plus the whole text block is pushed right, leaving a big empty area on the left, and the quote's last word 'move.' runs straight into the 'MONOGRAPH' wordmark, a clear collision.

A has a clean centred column, but the logo is shrunk to a tiny, illegible mark tucked in the bottom-left corner. The price now sits above the product name, which reverses the original reading order, and the stack leaves wide empty side margins on the square canvas. B is chaotic: the watch is pushed off-centre to the right, and the price, name, 'Free engraving' and Shop button each sit on a different axis. The logo floats at mid-left, unrelated to anything, and the bottom third of the canvas is dead space.

Both use the same flawed layout: the price sits above the supporting copy, so the original order is swapped. The 'Book a Fitting' button is oversized and competes with the headline. The Monograph logo shrinks to an unreadable speck in the bottom-left corner, and the legal block is too small to read and is crammed against the bottom edge. In B the larger watch's strap runs off both the top and bottom edges and crowds the logo. In A the strap is cut only at the top and ends cleanly above the logo, which gives A slightly more breathing room.

A: the logo floats off-centre to the right while the headline is left-aligned and the CTA is centred, so the three share no axis. The top-left is dead space, and the Book Now button is jammed against a sliver of sea with white specks right under it. B has the same mixed alignment and a CTA crammed against the bottom edge, and is worse in two ways: the white Meridian logo sits on pale sky with almost no contrast, so the brand is close to unreadable, and a large empty blue band separates it from the text block.

A keeps the original structure (logo stacked over headline and subcopy in a left column, CTA in the middle, products on the right), but the shrink is basically proportional. The logo and subcopy are tiny and unreadable at 320×50, and the CTA is jammed close to the bottle. B separates the tiny logo from the headline, leaving it stranded at the far left, centres the headline and subcopy with no shared edge, and crowds the CTA against the bottle and circle. Its subcopy is even smaller and also unreadable, so B is slightly worse.

The two layouts are almost the same, and both share the same flaws. The pink circle is no longer behind the bottle; it sits alone, cropped, in the bottom-right corner. The quote mark floats about 60px above its headline. The headline is set small on one line and loses out to the large bottle. The left-aligned text block clashes with the centred bottle and button. A is pushed up: the top feels cramped, and there is a dead gap of about 145px between the button and the logo. B moves the whole stack down, which balances the space top to bottom better, so it is slightly less lopsided.

A: the 'See the Study' button sits on top of the image's bottom edge, an unwanted collision. The legal block is jammed against the end of the headline with almost no gutter. The headline and subhead are indented differently from the eyebrow, so the left edges are ragged. The subhead is much bigger than the tiny CTA, the jar shrinks to a token icon, and the logo is pushed into the bottom corner. B: the left edges line up (eyebrow, headline, subhead and CTA/jar/logo row) and the legal copy sits in its own column, but the headline butts right against the image with no gutter. The subhead is cramped under the headline, the CTA is undersized and crowded next to a tiny jar and the logo, and the legal text is barely legible, but B has fewer collisions than A.

A: the quote mark, headline and source line share a clean left edge, but that block doesn't line up with the centred logo. It is also a vertical stack in the middle of a wide banner, with large empty areas on the left and right, and 'Rated 5 out of 5' is shrunk until it can't be read. B is worse: four different left edges (quote mark ~197, headline ~219, source ~197, rating ~160) look arbitrary, a large gap pulls the source line away from its quote, and 'Rated 5 out of 5' is again too small to read.

Both put "$3" above "2 FOR", so the offer reads backwards. Both also move the FIZZBANG logo from top-centre to an oversized pill crammed into the bottom-left corner, off the centre axis and nearly touching the left and bottom edges, and both leave dead pink space at the top. A edges ahead only because its can is slightly larger and has more presence; B shrinks the product further, so the hero image feels trivial.

Both share the same fatal flaws. The date card (SAT 22 NOV, the key event info) has shrunk to an unreadable yellow speck. The subcopy and the 'Fizzbang Arcade Night' kicker are microscopic. The CTA sits on the far left before the headline, so the reading order is backwards. The controller is a tiny orphan, and the FIZZBANG logo floats arbitrarily above the headline. A's cropped pattern panel also bleeds flush to the top, bottom and right edges. B gives that panel even margins and a slightly larger controller, which makes it marginally less cramped, but it is otherwise identical.

A keeps the original left-to-right strip with headline and subcopy on one left edge, but it reads as a stretched copy rather than a real reflow: a big gap separates the headline from its subcopy, the subcopy is tiny, the can is shrunk, and there's dead yellow above and below. B is worse: the enlarged headline floats in the top-left and doesn't line up with the subcopy (indented about 45px further right), and that same over-large gap pulls them apart. The can and controller sink to the bottom with an empty band above them, and the logo and CTA sit low on their own axis, so the layout looks bottom-heavy and arbitrary.

Both candidates have the same flaws. The Fizzbang can, which is key product imagery, is shrunk to an illegible thumbnail stuck to the bottom-left next to a tiny logo pill. That leaves a cramped footer cluster beside an empty bottom-right corner. Both CTAs are also slightly out of line with the text column's left edge. A's wider CTA holds the hierarchy better, while B's narrower, centred button is weaker and floats more arbitrarily, so A is marginally better.

A: the 'Pick Your Flavour' CTA is shrunk to an unreadable pill stuck in the bottom-left corner, cut off from everything else. The flavour list is out of the original order, its items shrink step by step and the dots form a ragged diagonal, and there is dead space under the copy. B has the same reordered, shrinking, ragged list and a can that dominates the frame, but its CTA is readable and sits just under the list, so the reading order of brand, headline, list then action survives.

A: the 'Try It' pill is pushed against the right canvas edge and its right end looks clipped, and the can is a tiny sliver with the yellow sun circle gone, so the left side looks weak next to the large headline. B: the CTA has a proper right margin and the can is slightly larger, but the CTA sits jammed right against 'Bang'. The yellow circle is also missing in B, and the subline is small for a 320x50 strip.

A: the white panel swallows almost the whole canvas and hides most of the pop-art shapes. The FIZZBANG! logo is pushed off the panel onto the busy pink circle and dark shape, cut off from the headline. The CTA is jammed against the right canvas edge with almost no margin. B: has the same oversized panel and lost graphics, and is slightly worse. Its logo straddles the yellow stripe and the panel edge in an accidental-looking collision, and it sits almost touching the headline. The cramped left cluster leaves dead white space on the right, though its CTA has a better margin.

A shrinks the logo pill to a small island in the middle of the wide strip, and the FIZZBANG! wordmark is jammed against the pill's outline with almost no padding, which breaks the logo's proportions. The SINCE 2026 badge is tiny and barely readable, and the sides are left empty. B keeps the wordmark's padding inside the pill and gives the logo real presence, but it is still just a centred stack with no use of the banner's width. B's pill nearly touches the top, the badge sits very close to the bottom edge, and the badge text is small.

A reflows the two-line headline onto one bold line that fills the strip and stays legible, but it is jammed against the canvas edges with almost no margin, so the airy, centred minimalism of the original is gone. B keeps the centred whitespace, but the headline is shrunk to tiny type that floats in a lot of empty space; it reads as a scaled-down copy with weak legibility at the target size.

The two layouts are almost identical, and both break the reading order. The black date block sits at the very top, above the headline, and the 'EXHIBITION' kicker has dropped below 'Concrete Poetry'. The opening-hours line inside the bar is unreadably small at this size, and there is a dead gap between the photo and the address. A wins narrowly because its date text is slightly larger, so the date block is a little more legible than B's even smaller type.

A keeps one left edge for logo, headline, list and CTA, and all four steps are the same size. Its flaws: the list text and CTA label are small for a tall canvas, the gaps between steps are loose and leave dead bands, and the jar sits low and to the right in a cropped circle. B breaks the list: step 1 is noticeably larger and indented compared with steps 2-4, so it looks like a mistake. Its logo, headline and list also start at different left edges, and the CTA label is tiny.

A: headline and subtitle share a clean left edge, but there is about 140px of dead space at the left and a large empty gap before the Shop Now button, which is stranded at the far right. The NEW badge has shrunk to an illegible speck under the subtitle, cut off from the product and jammed against the bottom edge, and the LUMEN & FIG label on the jar is unreadable. The NEW badge is the same tiny, detached speck crammed at the bottom edge, and the whole cluster floats in the middle with empty sides, so it reads as shrunk rather than laid out as a banner.

Both use the same sensible left-to-right strip layout: badge, jar, then 'Night Cream' headline with subcopy, and Shop Now on the right. Both have the same flaws: the NEW badge is cropped at the top, bottom and left canvas edges, and the subcopy is very small. A's jar is shrunk so far that the LUMEN & FIG label can't be read, and it floats in a gap. B's jar is a bit larger and sits closer to the badge, so the product has more presence. B is only marginally better: its jar crowds the badge and its brand label is still close to illegible.

Both share serious flaws: the 'MAYA R., VERIFIED BUYER' attribution is set larger and heavier than the quote, which inverts the hierarchy and crowds the line right under it; the blush circle is cut off and stranded in the bottom-right corner instead of sitting behind the bottle; and the quote mark floats with a large gap above the headline. A at least gives the logo its own top band. In B the logo drops down level with the quote mark, so the two crowd each other off-axis and leave an empty strip at the top.

A: the quote mark floats alone far above the quote, the CTA sits to the left of the quote on a different baseline so the reading order is backwards, the attribution is blown up almost as loud as the headline, the bottle is pulled away from its circle, and the logo crowds the circle's edge. B is worse: the CTA pill butts directly against 'MAYA R., VERIFIED BUYER' (a collision), the quote mark is stranded high, the bottle is split from its circle, which is cropped at the right edge under the logo, and the tiny bottle label is unreadable.

Both share the same flaws. The 'OBSIDIAN ONE' eyebrow was moved below the body copy and enlarged with wide tracking, so it competes with the headline and breaks the reading order. The logo is right-aligned while all the text is left-aligned. The headline, body and eyebrow are crammed together with almost no spacing between them. The dark card fills nearly the whole canvas and runs off the bottom, so the city skyline, a key image in the original, is reduced to thin slivers at the edges. B's slightly larger headphones fill the middle better and leave less dead space above the CTA than A's smaller ones, but the difference is marginal.

A and B look the same pixel for pixel. Both drop the city skyline and night sky, which loses the original's key imagery. Both push the body copy to the far left as a 5-line column too small to read, ahead of the headline, so the reading order is wrong. The headphones are cut off at the left edge, the OBSIDIAN logo is a tiny line under the headline, and the 'OBSIDIAN ONE' eyebrow is shrunk to an unreadable cyan dash. The headline and the 'Try a Pair' CTA are still legible and in the right order relative to each other.

The two layouts are essentially identical. The only difference I can see is that B's logo icon looks teal and A's looks grey, and I can't tell which matches the original. Both share the same flaws: the 'OBSIDIAN ONE' eyebrow has dropped below the body copy, which breaks the original reading order. The logo is tiny and right-aligned, while every other element is left-aligned. The city skyline, the key image, is cut down to a thin strip at the bottom, and the oversized 'Try a Pair' button sits in an empty gap below the headphones.

A keeps the OBSIDIAN logo at a readable size, but the logo floats near the canvas center instead of over the text column. The Shop button is pushed left of the centered headline/price axis, and there is dead space along the bottom. B gets the alignment right (headline, price and button share one center axis), but it shrinks the logo to an illegible ~5px wordmark, so the brand is effectively lost. A keeps the earbud case as a strong hero centered under the logo, but the headline is undersized for the wider canvas, and there are large empty bands between the product, the copy and the Shop button, plus dead space below the CTA. B uses the same text and CTA layout but shrinks the product to a small icon, so the key image no longer matters. That leaves a big empty gap above the headline and makes the layout feel even more sparse and unbalanced.

Both share the same serious flaws: the 'PICK YOUR SOUND' eyebrow is moved to the far right after the headline, which breaks the reading order. The price labels are swapped (Obsidian Buds $179 sits under the headphones, Obsidian One $349 sits beside a scrap of the earbuds case). The earbud case is cut down to two floating dots, the headphone band is cropped at the top, and an orphaned platform ellipse floats at the right edge. A at least left-aligns the headline with the subhead and price row. B's bigger headline sticks out about 40px left of the subhead, so its left edge is ragged, and it crowds the headphone graphic.

A: the eyebrow, headline and body share a left edge at x≈123, but the logo (x≈78) and the CTA (x≈83) sit off that edge. The body copy, logo and price labels are tiny and hard to read. The headphones lost their shadow plate while the buds kept theirs, and the buds float at the far bottom-right corner with their label on a different baseline from the headphone label. B shares the product-side flaws, and its left column is ragged throughout: the logo starts at x≈70, the eyebrow at x≈120, the headline at x≈62, the body at x≈117 and the CTA at x≈80. No two elements share an edge, so B is the more arbitrary of the two.

A has no shared left edge: the quote mark sits at about x=155, the headline at about x=152 and the attribution juts out to x=75. 'Rated 5 out of 5' floats in mid-canvas, the logo hangs in empty space mid-right instead of anchoring an edge, and the attribution crowds the bottom edge. B puts the quote mark, headline and attribution on one left edge with the rating grouped beside the attribution and the logo pinned right, but it still leaves a dead ~160px band on the left, shrinks the quote mark to a speck and leaves the headline small for the strip.

Neither candidate is a real resize. Both drop the original single-row strip (logo, headline, Shop button) unchanged into the middle of a tall portrait canvas, so about 90% of the frame is empty dark space. The headline stays small instead of becoming the dominant element, and nothing is rearranged into a top-to-bottom reading order. A is marginally better because its logo margin (~14px) nearly matches the button's right margin (~11px). B's logo sits ~27px in against an ~11px right margin, making the row visibly off-balance.

A shrinks the date card to an unreadable speck (the 'NOV 14 / FRI 7:30 PM' event info is effectively gone), the eyebrow and address line are microscopic, the headphone's backing circle is split off as an orphaned blob in the bottom-right, and large dead bands sit around a weak headline/CTA row. A: the bottle straddles the card's left edge, so it collides with the panel border. The 'NEW NIGHT SERUM' eyebrow floats under the body copy, off every alignment, which breaks the reading order. The CTA nearly touches the end of the headline. B: the bottle sits cleanly in the leaf panel, and the eyebrow lines up neatly in a row with the logo. B still has flaws: the CTA is jammed against 'skin', the eyebrow and logo are tiny at banner size, and the bottle label is barely legible.

Both share the same flaws: the 'NEW NIGHT SERUM' eyebrow drops below the body copy and the logo is pushed to the bottom (wrong reading order), the bottle is jammed against the top and bottom canvas edges, and the leaf background is reduced to scraps. A's text block sits more evenly within the card. B's text sits low, so the Lumen & Fig logo nearly touches the bottom of the card, and its CTA is pushed toward the right edge with a large empty gap in the middle, so A is marginally better.

A keeps the original structure: the quote, attribution, CTA and logo share a left edge, and the serum circle sits in the right column with a clear gap. Its only flaw is a slightly loose vertical rhythm with extra space under the logo. B moves the circle left until it almost touches the end of 'slept', which leaves dead space on the right. Its 'MAYA R., VERIFIED BUYER' line also sits about 8px left of the headline's edge, which breaks the alignment.

A: the CTA pill is pushed to the far-left edge, below the quote's baseline and almost touching its first word. The tiny quote mark floats on its own above the text, the attribution is centred under nothing in particular, and the logo sits on top of the circle, so the layout reads as scattered pieces. B: the CTA pill butts straight into 'MAYA R., VERIFIED BUYER' (a collision). The bottle is pulled off its circle and touches the top edge, the circle is cut off at the right edge with the logo on top of it, and the left 160px is dead space. Both are broken; A is slightly less colliding.

Both use the same layout and share the same flaws: the cream jar has shrunk to a tiny icon sitting right after 'wash.' like a stray emoji, the backdrop circle survives only as a cut-off sliver poking out behind the CTA's top-right corner, and 'THE NIGHT SET' and the 'Worth $72' line are too small to read at banner height. The serum bottle floats in a column with nothing around it, and the gap between it and the $48 block is wide and empty. The only visible difference is a slight change in the jar's position and lid tint, so neither is better.

Both are almost the same leaderboard layout. The headline reads well. Two things are clearly broken: a dense legal block takes the right quarter at an unreadable ~5px, and the 'CLINICALLY TESTED' eyebrow has moved down to the bottom row after the logo, which breaks the reading order. The CTA, logo and jar are crammed into one small cluster on the bottom row, and the leaf strip on the left is a cropped scrap. B is very slightly better because its jar keeps more of its green lid, so it is easier to recognise. In A the jar shrinks to a pale smudge.

Both scramble the reading order the same way. The 'PICK YOUR SOUND' eyebrow is oversized and sits below the headline. The 'Obsidian One, $349' caption floats above it, cut off from the headphones. The 'Obsidian Buds, $179' label and the Compare Models CTA sit above the headphones' grey shadow disc, while the buds and their disc are stranded at the bottom, so the product, price and CTA groupings are broken and the CTA is buried mid-canvas. A is slightly worse: its body copy is indented off the headline's left edge, while B keeps the body aligned with the headline. Otherwise they are nearly identical.

Both use the same broken layout. The spec grid is broken up and scattered: 40 h and BT 5.4 sit on top of the teal circle and get in the way of the tagline, while 10 min, 250 g, -38 dB and 6 mics float in random places. The tagline is jammed against the logo and the headline. The legal line is set as large as body copy, and the circle no longer holds the headphones. They differ only in the logo: A's is a bit larger and easier to read, while B's is tiny and close to illegible.

A: the headline is shrunk to small italic text that the logo outweighs. It starts at a different left edge (~205px) from the source and rating lines (~108px), so the alignment is ragged. The tiny quote mark floats alone far from the logo, and the right third of the canvas is dead space. B: the headline, source and rating share one left edge, and the quote mark sits above the headline. That is better grouping, but the headline is still tiny, smaller in visual weight than the oversized logo. The logo is centred on its own axis instead of the text column, the text block is crammed with almost no line spacing, and the right half is empty.

Both keep the original's single horizontal row and barely enlarge it for the much taller canvas, so the headline and CTA sit in a thin band with large empty areas above and below. This reads as a stretched strip rather than a rearranged layout, and the headline is undersized for the format. A is marginally better: its logo sits about 24px from the left edge, which roughly matches the CTA's ~20px right margin. B's logo is enlarged and pushed to about 13px from the left edge, which looks cramped and makes the side margins uneven.

Neither candidate rearranges anything. Both drop the original single-row strip unchanged into the middle of a portrait canvas, leaving about 85% of it as empty dark space above and below. The headline stays strip-sized, so it lacks the presence a portrait layout needs, and the Shop button sits about 15px from the right edge. A also has lopsided side margins (logo about 38px in from the left, button about 15px from the right). B's margins are slightly more even (about 20px left, 15px right) but just as cramped against the edges, so it wins only on that minor point.

A: the logo is pushed hard against the left edge (~12px margin, while the Shop button sits ~20px from the right) and rides about 15px above the shared centre line of headline and button, so the row looks misaligned. It is also oversized next to the headline. B: the logo sits on the same centre axis with a better left margin. But both just spread the strip's single row across a much taller canvas, leaving large empty bands above and below, and the Shop button still crowds the right edge.

Both break up the text column the same way: the eyebrow floats about 70px above the headline, there is a large dead gap between the headline, the body copy and the RSVP button, and in both the headphone illustration has come apart, with the headband and cups sitting above the dark circle instead of inside it. A is worse: the date card is oversized and jammed 22px from the left edge, and the circle almost touches the bottom edge, so it looks cramped and cropped. B keeps the date card in proportion with better margins and a more contained circle, but it still has the scattered spacing and the broken graphic.

A and B look pixel-identical. In both, the Meridian logo has shrunk to a tiny mark tucked next to the CTA instead of leading the layout. The supporting copy is squeezed into a narrow 5-line column jammed against the right edge, at an illegible size with an orphan 'summer.'. The sunglasses float in the top-left corner, away from the suitcase, and the original's light-blue circle behind the suitcase is gone.

A: the CTA sits at the top above the logo and headline, so the reading order is backwards. The Reykjavik card is stranded alone and smaller than the other two, the cards follow no grid, and the subcopy is wedged under the Lisbon card, leaving the right half empty. B has the same broken order and scattered layout, but its three fare cards are shrunk so far that the city names and 'from' labels can't be read, and most of the canvas is dead navy space, so it's worse.

The two layouts are almost the same: the suitcase is on the left without its pale circle backdrop, the logo is demoted to the bottom-left corner under the suitcase's wheels, and the legal block is shrunk to unreadable micro-type. A is worse because the headline 'Fly now,' is jammed against the top edge with almost no margin, so the top-right feels cramped while the space below the legal text is loose. B gives the headline proper top breathing room and spaces the headline, subhead and CTA more evenly, but it still has the buried logo, the suitcase crowding the left edge and illegible fine print.

A keeps the quote mark, headline, attribution and rating on one left edge (only the logo is slightly indented), but the headline is undersized for the tall canvas, the gaps between the headline and attribution and between the attribution and rating are too loose, and the attribution and rating text is tiny. B has the same small type, and its left edges are ragged: the quote mark sits at about x80, the headline at x56, the attribution at x43 and the logo at x55. It also leaves a large dead area below the logo, which makes the layout top-heavy and look arbitrary.

The two layouts are nearly identical, and both share the same flaws. The suitcase almost touches the left edge and has lost its circle backdrop. The Meridian logo has dropped to the bottom-left corner under the suitcase, so the brand comes last instead of leading. The legal text is crammed into a block of about 4px type that nobody can read. The headline and subcopy also run almost to the right edge. A is slightly better because its 'How It Works' button is a little larger and more prominent. B's text column starts further left and its button is smaller, which makes the right column feel more cramped.

Both have the same serious flaws. The MONOGRAPH logo is shrunk to an unreadable speck and dropped awkwardly at the base of the watch, which is a brand failure. The price also sits above 'Field Watch No. 2', so the original reading order is reversed. The watch hugs the left edge, leaving a large dead gap. A pushes the Shop button out to the far right edge, cut off from its copy. B moves Shop closer to the price/title block, which groups the CTA better, so B is slightly less bad.

Both break the schedule apart. Only the 02 Dec row stays readable, and it sits at the top beside the legal line. The other rows are scattered as microscopic fragments around the CTA, the logo is shrunk into the bottom-left corner, and the WINTER PROGRAMME kicker is gone. A jams its CTA right under 'studios' and beside the Bookbinding fragment; B gives the CTA more room under the headline but insets the image off the headline's left edge, so B is only marginally less cramped.

Both are nearly the same broken skyscraper: the six-session schedule is split up and out of order (13 Jan/09 Dec/20 Jan crammed at the top, 16 Dec stuck under the headline, 06 Jan below the CTA), so the dates are tiny and the order is lost. In both, the oversized CTA pill crowds the rows above and below it, and the logo and fine print end up in a cramped footer. B is slightly worse: its headline and image are wider and run nearer the canvas edges, its CTA nearly fills the full width, and stray micro-text by the logo adds clutter. A keeps marginally better side margins.

A: the blue panel is centred, but the Meridian logo floats off-axis to the right over light sky, where it has weak contrast. Inside the panel there is too much empty space, and the Book Now button sits right of centre, out of line with the left-aligned headline and subline. B: the panel is shoved left, leaving a 164px strip of empty sea on the right, and it is not aligned with the canvas-centred logo above it. The button again floats off the text's left edge, and the panel nearly touches the bottom of the canvas. A is slightly better balanced, so it wins narrowly.

Both break the same way. The white card fills the canvas edge to edge with no margin. The CTA sits above the headline, which reverses the reading order. A large empty white band splits the content, and the desert shrinks to a strip with the sun gone. A is slightly worse: the logo floats lower than the CTA, so the two don't line up, and the CTA doesn't share the headline's left edge. In B the logo and CTA sit on one row, but B's CTA is still misaligned with the headline, and both B's CTA and its text sit closer to the edges.

Both reorder the copy to '$199 / New York / from', which breaks the original 'New York from $199' message. Both also shrink the headline, the tiny 'from' and the Book CTA to near-insignificance and drop the logo to the bottom-left so it no longer leads. A is worse: its whole column sits off-centre to the right (axis about x=240 on a 432 canvas), leaving a lopsided empty left side and a large dead band at the top. B at least centres the column, though its logo crowds the bottom-left edge and the oversized suitcase still outweighs the text.

Both use the same broken layout. The three price cards are scattered (Reykjavik stranded alone up top, Marrakech and Lisbon at the bottom), their order is reversed from the original, and the card city names and 'from' labels are illegibly tiny. The subtitle floats between the cards, cut off from its headline, and the logo is pushed down to the bottom corner. A is slightly worse because the Marrakech and Lisbon cards butt into or overlap each other; B keeps a small gap and slightly cleaner spacing.

A: the oversized Meridian logo runs into the blue panel's left edge (the final 'n' touches or is clipped by it). The CTA and 40% badge are shrunk to tiny chips, and the glasses illustration sits jammed beside them in the panel. There is an awkward dead gap between headline and subcopy, and the panel's bottom area is empty. B has the same flaws: an oversized logo next to a tiny CTA and badge, with the glasses moved into the panel. Its panel is also jammed against the top and right canvas edges and the logo nearly touches the left edge. But the logo clears the panel and the headline-to-subcopy spacing is tighter, so B is marginally less broken.

Both are near-identical straight shrinks of the original into a 320x50 strip. The logo wordmark, the subline and the CTA label are a few pixels tall and can't be read, and the products are crammed against the right edge with the circle cropped. A centres the headline and subline away from the logo, so they don't share a left edge. B keeps logo, headline and subline on one left axis like the original, which makes it slightly tidier.

Both make the same mistakes. The headline quote is shrunk to one small line that runs nearly edge to edge, so it no longer leads the layout and the bottle dominates. The quote mark floats far above its text, and the pink circle has come loose from the bottle and sits stranded, cut off in the bottom-right corner. A spreads the stack more evenly down the canvas, with some empty space at the top. B pushes everything up, which leaves a large dead gap between the CTA and the logo, so A is slightly better.

A: the headline and subhead sit flush against the leaf image with no gutter. The logo and the jar are shrunk to tiny chips crammed along the bottom edge beside the CTA. The legal text floats in a separate column far to the right with a dead gap, but the left text column at least shares one clean left edge. B is worse: the headline is indented away from the eyebrow and subhead, so the left edge is ragged. 'calmer' almost touches the legal column, the CTA overlaps the bottom corner of the image, and the CTA, jar and logo sit on different baselines, so the bottom row reads as scattered.

Both are nearly the same broken layout: the yellow date card ('SAT 22 NOV, 8PM–1AM') has shrunk to an unreadable speck, so the event date is lost. The 'Pier 9 Arcade…' and 'FIZZBANG ARCADE NIGHT' lines are microscopic, and the CTA floats on the far left away from the headline, which breaks the reading order. B's cropped pattern panel runs almost to the top and bottom canvas edges and looks jammed. A keeps a small margin around the panel, so it is marginally cleaner.

Both have the same structural problems. The white card runs into the top, left and right canvas edges, so the original's inset rounded panel is lost and the dune art shrinks to a thin strip. The See Fares CTA sits above the headline, which breaks the reading order. A big empty white gap separates the CTA/logo from the headline, and the CTA's left edge doesn't line up with the headline. A is slightly less bad because the CTA and logo at least share one row. In B they are staggered at different heights for no reason, which adds another misalignment and makes the top look scattered.

Both scatter the three fare cards into a disjointed zigzag, put them in reverse order (Reykjavik first, Lisbon last), wedge the subcopy between cards away from the headline, and shrink the city names and 'from' labels until they can't be read. B is worse: the Lisbon card overlaps the Marrakech card, and the Meridian logo mark crowds or overlaps its wordmark. A at least keeps the cards apart and the logo intact.

A: the offer reads backwards, with '$3' stacked above '2 FOR', and the FIZZBANG logo pill is shrunk to an illegible chip under '2 FOR' instead of leading the design. The can is tiny and jammed against the left edge, and the '$3' is too small to be the hero. B makes the same mistakes: '2 FOR' trails '$3' and sits at an offset baseline, and the logo is again a tiny chip, this time crowded against the Find a Store button. Its 'Every flavour, all week long' line is larger than the price, so the secondary copy becomes the focal point, which is slightly worse hierarchy than A.

The two banners are almost pixel-identical and share the same flaws. The five-item flavour list is broken up and scattered: 'Cherry Bang' and 'Mango Boom' are large in the centre, while 'Lime Zap' and 'Grape Pop' are tiny and wedged above and below the CTA, and 'Cola Crash' sits alone at the bottom-left under the logo. The list is out of order, its type sizes are inconsistent, and the colour dots are mismatched. The small labels, logo and can are unreadable at this height, and the logo badge is cramped against the top-left edge. In both, the headline and CTA keep reasonable prominence, but the middle of the banner is a jumble of fragments rather than a left-to-right read.

The two candidates are practically the same. Both turn the design into a left-to-right leaderboard with a readable headline and a clear pink CTA. In both, the FIZZBANG! logo pill is jammed against the cropped pop-art shapes and sits on top of the yellow stripe, so the logo is crowded and the artwork has a busy collision behind it. In both, the geometric art is cut down to a cramped sliver at the left edge, a thin blue strip at the right edge looks accidental, and the CTA text is small, so the pop-art feel of the original is mostly lost.

In both, the white card covers almost the whole canvas, so the pop-art shapes that define the brand shrink to slivers at the edges. Both also break the headline badly, leaving 'can' alone on its own line, and the FIZZBANG logo pill is oversized and competes with the headline. B is slightly worse because its CTA sits right against the bottom edge of the card and canvas, while A keeps a little room below the button.

A keeps the pill wordmark at a usable size, but the 'FIZZBANG!' text, especially the '!', is jammed against the pill outline, and the 'SINCE 2026' badge nearly touches the bottom edge. It is still a centred stack rather than a layout built for the banner. B has the same crowded '!' inside a pill shrunk to about a fifth of the width, so the brand mark is weak and flanked by large empty halftone areas, and the badge text is tiny and hard to read at this size.

A: the FIZZBANG! pill runs almost the full canvas width with only about 4px of margin, so it feels jammed against the edges. The SINCE 2026 badge is nearly as wide and heavy as the pill, which weakens the hierarchy, though the group sits near the vertical centre. B: the pill has proper side margins and the smaller badge is clearly subordinate, but the group sits low (around 55–80% of the height), leaving the top half as empty halftone. B is still closer to the original's lower-centre placement and spacing. Neither one rearranges the layout for the tall format; both just scale the pair down.

A blows the headline up to nearly the full banner height, leaving only about 30px above and below it against roughly 165px at the sides. That makes it vertically cramped and loses the generous whitespace that defines the original's quiet 'silence' feel. B keeps the centred two-line serif headline with balanced breathing room close to the original's proportions and is still clearly legible. Its flaws are minor: the type is a bit small for the wide banner, and neither candidate reflows the line to suit the wide format.

A: the headline sits right against the cropped photo, and the 'EXHIBITION' label has moved from above the title to the end of the address line, which breaks the reading order. The logo has shrunk to an illegible speck, and there is dead space on the right. Still, its date block is a usable size. B has the same reading-order and logo problems, but its date block is shrunk until the hours line can't be read. The headline's 'C' runs into the photo's edge, and the photo is pushed hard against the left edge of the canvas while about a quarter of the canvas on the right sits empty.

A: the big quote mark that anchored the original has shrunk to a tiny glyph floating above the text, the left ~170px is dead space, and the logo's MONOGRAPH/GALLERY wordmark is shrunk and crowded until it is barely legible. Still, the quote and attribution share a left edge and read in order. B has all of A's problems and is worse: the attribution starts about 45px left of the quote, so nothing lines up, the quote mark floats over the middle of the line, and the logo wordmark is cut off at the bottom edge of the canvas (GALLERY is clipped), which breaks the brand.

Both shrink the Monograph logo to an illegible speck, so the brand is effectively lost, and both stack the price above the title, which flips the original reading order. In A the logo floats arbitrarily between the watch and the text, though the Shop button sits centred on the text block and is grouped with it. In B the logo is pushed into the bottom-left corner beside the watch, and the Shop button is pinned high near the right edge, lined up with the price rather than the block, which leaves its edge margin cramped and the right side unbalanced.

A keeps a clean centred stack with comfortable margins, but the logo is shrunk to an illegible thumbnail in the bottom-left corner, so the brand is effectively lost. The $420 also sits above the 'Field Watch No. 2' headline, flipping the reading order, and the text block is tight. B keeps a readable logo but jams it against the headline. The price, headline and 'Free engraving' sit on different centre lines, the watch strap touches the top edge and the Shop button is cropped at the bottom edge, so B looks cramped and unintentional.

Both break the TUE/WED/THU list into fragments: TUE sits at far left, WED under the headline and THU beside the logo. TUE and THU are tiny, almost unreadable text, and the logo's GALLERY line disappears. A is worse because the WED row is set much larger than TUE and THU, so the list has inconsistent sizes and the row competes with the headline, and it is jammed against 'All free, all at 19:00.' B at least keeps all three rows the same size and leaves space between WED and the subline.

Both scramble the copy into '$199 / New York / from', so 'from' now dangles under the city and reads like nonsense. Both also shrink the headline, price and Book CTA to small type lost in a mostly empty blue field. A at least keeps one centred column with even vertical rhythm and the logo in its own footer corner, though about 140px of dead space sits on top. B pushes the whole stack about 18px right of centre. Its logo sits on the same row as the Book button, so the two compete side by side, and the bottom fifth is left empty, which makes B lopsided and less intentional.

A: the Meridian logo has shrunk to an illegible speck, 'from' sits by itself under the logo, and '$199' and 'New York' are staggered on different baselines, so the line reads in a jumbled order. B: '$199' and 'New York' are stacked cleanly as one centred group, but the logo is still a tiny unreadable mark jammed into 'from' at the bottom edge, and the Book button is pressed against the right edge. B is slightly less broken because its price block is grouped together.

Both have the same broken reading order: '$199' sits above 'New York', 'from' comes after the price, and the Meridian logo is shrunk to an illegible sliver jammed between 'New York' and 'from', so the brand is effectively lost. B is worse because its Book button runs into the right, top and bottom canvas edges and gets cut off, and its logo mark turns dark and low-contrast on the blue. A at least keeps some margin around the CTA.

Both put the 'How It Works' CTA at the top, above the headline, which breaks the reading order. Both cut the decorative circle off from the suitcase and leave it in the top-right corner, where it crowds the Meridian logo and touches the end of the headline. Both shrink the legal text to an unreadable size and leave a large empty band above it. A keeps a more comfortable 42px left margin, but its suitcase sits slightly right of centre. B's 25px margin is cramped against the canvas edge, though its suitcase is centred. They are otherwise almost identical, so A wins by a small margin.

Both make the same structural mistakes. The 'How It Works' CTA is moved above the headline, which breaks the reading order. The Meridian logo is pushed top-right and straddles the edge of the decorative white circle. The circle no longer frames the suitcase and instead sits behind the end of the headline, where 'four' runs into it. The legal text is tiny. A also has a tight 32px left margin and a smaller suitcase that leaves more dead space above the legal text. B has slightly better margins and a larger suitcase that fills the space better, but its legal text sits close to the bottom edge.

Both share the same broken structure: the Meridian logo has been pulled out of the blue panel onto the busy photo, and its 'n' butts into the panel edge. The sunglasses are cropped at the top-left, and the panel is jammed against the top of the canvas. A's 'Find a Fare' CTA spills past the panel's bottom-right corner and crowds the badge. B keeps the CTA inside the panel, but it shrinks to an illegible pill jammed against the end of the body copy, and the badge text is also smaller. A's CTA is at least readable.

Both lose every price, the actual offer. They scatter the six city rows as tiny fragments: some float in a white strip on the left, and Berlin and Madrid sit as dark navy text on the blue panel where they can't be read. The legal line is also illegible on blue, the CTA hangs off the edge of the offset blue panel, and white margins leave the canvas looking unfinished. B is slightly worse because its larger 'Madrid' crowds the legal line and the panel leaves white gaps on three sides, while A's leftovers are at least smaller and less distracting.

A: the jar, text and CTA form one centred group, but the headline is centred while the subcopy starts further left, so the text block has a ragged left edge. The NEW badge has shrunk to an illegible speck jammed against the bottom edge, below the subcopy instead of beside the product, and there are large empty strips at both ends. B: the headline and subcopy share a clean left edge, but the layout is lopsided. There is about 140px of dead space on the left, Shop Now is pushed hard against the right edge (about 25px margin), and a wide gap cuts the CTA off from its copy. The same tiny NEW badge sits at the bottom edge here too.

The two are nearly identical. Both move the small 'OBSIDIAN ONE' label below the body copy and blow it up into a loud second headline, which breaks the reading order and the hierarchy. Both also right-align the logo against left-aligned text, jam the body copy under the headline, and let the dark card cover almost all of the city skyline, so the key imagery is mostly lost. A's slightly larger headphones fill the middle better than B's smaller ones, which leave a looser gap above the CTA.

A: the right-hand text column is neatly centred, but the OBSIDIAN logo is shrunk so far that the wordmark can't be read, which hurts the brand. The column also sits high, leaving dead space at the bottom, and the earbuds case floats at the left without a clear relationship to it. B: the logo stays readable and the headline is larger with stronger hierarchy. However, the Shop button is neither centred under the copy nor aligned to the headline's left edge, and the headline runs close to the right edge. B is the better resize because it keeps the brand intact, which A does not.

Both share the same serious flaws. The 'Pick your sound' eyebrow is moved to the far right, after the headline, so the reading order is wrong. The earbuds case is reduced to two dots stuck between the CTA and a label. The product labels no longer sit with their products ('Obsidian Buds, $179' is under the headphones, 'Obsidian One' is beside the bud dots). An orphaned empty grey ellipse floats at the right. A's headline is a little larger but crowds right up against the headphones, while B leaves a cleaner gap between the headphones and the copy block, so B is marginally better.

Both break the five-flavour list into scattered pieces: Cherry Bang and Mango Boom sit big in the middle, Cola Crash is stranded under the logo at far left, and Lime Zap and Grape Pop are crammed in at tiny, unreadable sizes around the CTA. That destroys the list's order and grouping and leaves competing focal points; the can is also tiny and the 'FIZZBANG!' logo pill is cramped at the edge. B is nearly identical but makes Mango Boom larger than Cherry Bang, which makes the flavour sizes even more inconsistent, so A is marginally less bad.

Both blow the white card up to nearly fill the canvas, so the pop-art shapes shrink to meaningless slivers at the edges and the brand feel is mostly lost. Both also wrap the headline badly, leaving 'can' as an orphan. A packs the logo, headline and CTA tightly, and its CTA sits almost on the card's bottom edge. B has slightly more even vertical spacing and a bit more room under the CTA, but the same structural flaws.

Both break up the schedule list. TUE sits far left, WED sits under the headline, and THU is jammed to the right of the logo, so the day order and grouping are lost. The TUE and THU lines are also illegibly tiny. A keeps the WED row at the same small scale as the others and leaves a gap before 'All free, all at 19:00'. B enlarges only the WED row, which makes the three items inconsistent and creates a competing focal point. B also crams 'All free, all at 19:00.' right against 'Drawing by hand in 2026', so they read as one run-on line.

A leaves a large dead band across the top while the CTA, logo pill and can are pushed down against the bottom edge, so the bottom row looks cramped. Its CTA is also tiny next to the headline. B centres the text block vertically, keeps margins even and leaves room under the action row, but it shares the same flaws: the 'Top Up Now' button is undersized, the can is shrunk to a thumbnail and crammed in beside the logo pill, and the upscaled controller has jagged, pixelated edges.

Both have the same faults: the yellow sun-circle is shrunk to a small blob that collides with the Try It button and is cut off at the top-right edge, the can is tiny and stranded far left (its FIZZ BANG label is unreadable), and the middle has wide dead gaps. A is worse because its tagline is left-shifted and doesn't line up with the Cherry Bang headline. B centres the tagline under the headline, so the copy block is aligned.

A keeps the original's centred, quiet composition, with the headline rewrapped to three lines on the vertical centre; its only flaw is that the type could be a bit larger, since it fills only about 55% of the width. B uses the same three-line wrap but drops the block into the lower half (about 52–77% of the height), leaving the top half empty and making the off-centre placement look accidental rather than intended.

A sets the headline on one line, centred on the horizontal axis, at a strong size for the banner, with even side margins; the one flaw is that it sits a little high, so the top margin is tighter than the bottom. B's headline is noticeably smaller and shifted left of centre (about x 172–522 on a 768 canvas), which leaves an uneven large empty area on the right and weakens the one statement that carries the whole design.

Both 320x50 strips just shrink the original: the quote is about 8px, and the 'AIKO TANABE, ARCHITECT' line is an illegible grey smear. In A the M logo is oversized and pushed to the bottom edge, so it competes with the quote and the 'GALLERY' line looks clipped. B keeps the logo lockup whole and subordinate, but its wordmark is microscopic, so B is only slightly less bad.

A: headline, body and CTA share one left edge, but the 'NOW OPEN' eyebrow now sits after the CTA, which breaks the reading order, and the button touches it with no gap. The logo floats on the busy photo strip and its tiny tagline is unreadable. B has the same eyebrow-after-CTA problem plus worse faults: the MONOGRAPH wordmark straddles the white panel edge (a collision), the body copy is indented from the headline (ragged alignment), and 'NOW OPEN' floats loose to the right of the button.

A keeps the original structure cleanly. Its flaws are minor left-edge drift: the schedule column sits at about x58 while the headline is at about x51 and the CTA at about x47, and the times column stops short of the image's right edge. B breaks the schedule: the first row (02 DEC / Printmaking / 18:00) is enlarged and runs to both canvas edges, so it touches them and falls out of line with the other five rows. B's enlarged image also crowds that row, and its CTA sits at x38, out of line with the headline.

Both are the same broken leaderboard. The schedule is scattered across the strip in random sizes and out of date order (13 JAN at the top, 02 DEC in the middle, 20 JAN at the bottom), with some rows illegibly tiny and some overlapping other text. The fine print sits large in the top-left as if it were the message, and the logo is shrunk to a speck next to the dates. A's headline and CTA are a little larger, while B's logo sits slightly further from the dates. Neither difference changes the verdict: both are unusable.

A: the Meridian logo is placed so its wordmark runs into the left edge of the white card, an unintended collision, and the blue logo sits on busy orange dunes with weak contrast. The 'See Fares' pill is shrunk to a tiny button with near-illegible text, and the card's padding is uneven. B: it has the same tiny, barely readable CTA and the blue-on-orange logo, and the logo is jammed against the left canvas edge, leaving an awkward gap before the card. However, nothing collides and the card reads cleanly from headline to subcopy to button, so B is the less broken of the two.

A: the copy reads out of order ('$199 / New York / from'), the Book button is jammed against the suitcase wheels, the Meridian logo has shrunk to an illegible speck in the bottom-left corner, and the single centred column leaves both sides of the wide canvas empty. B has all of those problems and is worse: $199 floats far above its copy, 'from' is offset from 'New York' instead of sharing its axis, and the Book button sits off-centre under the suitcase, so nothing lines up.

Both are nearly identical leaderboard resizes with the same problems. The headline is dropped between the price cards, so the Reykjavik card is cut off from Lisbon and Marrakech and the group is broken up. The cards are thumbnail-sized, so the city names and 'from' labels are unreadable, and the Reykjavik card is larger than the other two. The logo is jammed against the top-left edge. The CTA and subcopy are tiny and sit cramped under the headline. B is marginally better because its headline's left edge lines up with the CTA, while A's headline sits a little left of it.

Both put the 'How It Works' CTA at the top above the headline, so the reading order is reversed. In both, the backdrop circle is pulled away from the suitcase and sits behind the logo as a stray blob. The legal text is shrunk past legibility and there are large dead gaps around the suitcase. B is a bit worse because its text column is jammed against the left edge (~17px margin vs ~30px in A), which makes it lopsided, while A's margins breathe slightly better even though its suitcase sits a little off-centre.

Both break the fare list: Madrid sits on the blue header's bottom edge with its $49 price missing, the legal line is wedged mid-list between London and Paris, the city order is scrambled, and a large empty band sits under the CTA. A is worse because Berlin is pushed to the canvas edge with an oversized $88 price that breaks the column, and its sub-labels are illegibly small. B at least keeps the rows on one consistent indent and price column, though its city and date text is tiny and the list is inset with ragged margins.

Both leave an unexplained white strip above the blue header, which looks like a mistake, and the legal line is tiny. A otherwise keeps one clean left edge (~32px) for the logo, headline, fare list, CTA and legal text, with matching right margins on the prices. B breaks that grid: the city/price list sits about 14px from the canvas edges while the headline is at ~32px and the CTA and legal text are at ~22px, so nothing aligns and the list feels jammed against the sides.

A: the 'MAYA R., VERIFIED BUYER' line has slipped left to about x=100, so it no longer lines up with the headline and CTA at x=108. The circle has been pulled inward to sit fully inside the canvas, which leaves a dead strip on the right, and the bottle sits off the circle's centre. B keeps the original's alignment, with quote, attribution, CTA and logo all on one left edge, and keeps the circle bleeding off the right edge as in the original. Its only flaw is slightly loose vertical spacing around the logo.

A: the headline has shrunk to roughly the size of the attribution and no longer stands out. The quote mark is tiny, the logo floats off-axis above the left-aligned text block, and the right half of the canvas is dead space. B is worse: it has three unrelated left edges (the quote mark and headline at about x=205, the attribution and rating at about x=108, the logo at about x=455). The attribution and rating are almost as large as the headline, and the logo outweighs the headline, so the hierarchy is inverted. The stray quote mark sits detached from the headline, with a large gap between it and the logo.

A keeps logo, headline and Shop button on one shared horizontal centre line, but it is a stretched strip copy: the content is undersized for the 192px height, with large empty bands above and below, the headline is too small to lead, and the button nearly touches the right edge (tighter than the left margin). B has the same empty bands and small headline, and its OBSIDIAN logo is also lifted about 18px above the axis the headline and button share, which reads as a placement error.

A: the logo floats outside the card on the busy orange dunes, low-contrast and jammed against the left edge; the See Fares CTA has shrunk to a tiny pill that is hard to read; the card is cropped at the canvas top and bottom. B has the same tiny CTA and cropped card, and is worse because the Meridian logo collides with the card's left edge, the wordmark running into the white panel, while a dead empty strip sits to its left.

Both are nearly the same broken leaderboard. The logo is jammed against the left edge, and the three fare cards are shrunk until the city names and 'from' labels can't be read. The cards are also split apart, with the headline wedged between Marrakech and Reykjavik, so the row of offers no longer reads as one group, and the subline is tiny next to the CTA. A keeps all three cards the same size. B makes the Reykjavik card wider and taller than the other two, which adds an inconsistency, so A is slightly less bad.
